newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican union boss to leave hospital soon.
newsitem.headline: Mexican union boss to leave hospital soon.

text.p: Powerful Mexican union boss Fidel Velazquez, 96, hospitalized since Tuesday with a lung infection, could be sent home as early as Friday, his doctor said on Thursday.

For 54 years, Velazquez has led the Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM), providing labour stability for nine Mexican presidents by aligning the seven million-strong CTM with the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).

His latest illness has come at a delicate time for the government as it prepares for annual negotiations with workers and employers on a new economic programme for 1997. Velazquez has no obvious successor at the CTM.
"His spirits are excellent, just as is his appetite," Dr Salomon Jasqui, the union leader's personal physician, told Reuters. "He could leave (the hospital) tomorrow or Saturday."
